rationale: C08 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both orders establish a named Federal council as an advisory body concerned with protecting Federal employees, place it under a cabinet-level administrative authority, define its membership or governance, authorize officers and committees, and revoke an earlier order establishing a predecessor council. The close correspondence in language and administrative machinery is substantially more specific than a generic shared practice of creating advisory bodies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Federal Fire Council, hereinafter referred to as the Council, is hereby established in the General Services Administration, as an official advisory agency in matters relating to the protection of Federal employees and property from fire.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby established in the Department of Labor the Federal Safety Council, hereinafter referred to as the Council, to serve in an advisory capacity to the Secretary of Labor in matters relating to the safety of civilian employees of the Federal Government
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the parent's establishment formula, defined term, departmental placement, advisory status, and Federal-employee protection mission to fire protection.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The functions of the Council shall be performed under the direction and supervision of the Administrator of General Services.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Labor shall prescribe appropriate regulations governing the activities and functions of the Council, and shall designate the Chairman thereof.
shared_material.explanation: Both place the council's functions under the responsible department head, with the supervising official changed to match the new institutional location.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Chairman shall appoint such other officers and committees as he may deem necessary to carry out the functions of the Council.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Council may choose such other officers, and establish such committees as it finds necessary for carrying out its functions.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close substantive and verbal adaptation of the same internal-governance clause.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] and No. 9594 are hereby revoked.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 21, 1939, establishing the Federal interdepartmental Safety Council, is hereby revoked.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by revoking prior directives governing a predecessor council, reinforcing the parallel administrative design.
